title: Listen well, say what you need, and say no kindly

say: Listen well, say what you need, and say no kindly.
This is the video for Module 2 of Communication and Self-Expression: guided practice.
People are far more willing to hear your view after they feel you have heard theirs. So first, you will listen actively.

panel.heading: Hear others, then be heard
items: Listen so people feel truly heard
Say a feeling and a need without blame
Say no and keep the relationship

say: Then you will express a feeling and a need without blame, using four steps.

panel.heading: Hear others, then be heard
items: Listen so people feel truly heard
Say a feeling and a need without blame

say: And you will practise saying no while protecting the relationship. Every unwilling yes is a no to something else, like your rest or your savings.

say: Step one. Attend. Put the phone face down, turn towards the person, and use small encouragers like, mm, I see, go on. Soft, occasional eye contact is fine with an elder.

panel.heading: Four moves of a good listener
items: Attend: phone down, turn towards her
Paraphrase the main point in your words
Ask open questions: what, how, tell me
Summarise and check: did I miss anything?

say: Step two. Paraphrase. Say back the main point in your own words. So the supplier delivered late twice, and now you are worried. You are checking, not agreeing yet.

panel.heading: Four moves of a good listener
items: Attend: phone down, turn towards her
Paraphrase the main point in your words
Ask open questions: what, how, tell me
Summarise and check: did I miss anything?

say: Step three. Ask open questions. What worries you most about it? Questions that get only yes or no are just for checking facts.

panel.heading: Four moves of a good listener
items: Attend: phone down, turn towards her
Paraphrase the main point in your words
Ask open questions: what, how, tell me
Summarise and check: did I miss anything?

say: Step four. Summarise the main points and ask, did I miss anything?

panel.heading: Four moves of a good listener
items: Attend: phone down, turn towards her
Paraphrase the main point in your words
Ask open questions: what, how, tell me
Summarise and check: did I miss anything?

say: The common mistakes are interrupting, fixing too fast, and turning to your own story. When you disagree, summarise her point before you reply.

panel.heading: Four moves of a good listener
items: Attend: phone down, turn towards her

Summarise and check: did I miss anything?
panel.rule: Understanding is not the same as agreeing.

say: The psychologist Marshall Rosenberg developed Nonviolent Communication, or NVC. It starts by removing blame.
A judgement adds your interpretation. You are lazy. You never help me. Words like always and never make people defend themselves.

panel.heading: Observation, not judgement
left: 'You never help me in the shop'
right: Last night's plates still in the sink
Came on two of four Saturdays

say: An observation is what a video camera would record. The plates from last night were still in the sink this morning. It is hard to argue with.
And name a real feeling. I feel ignored accuses. I feel lonely and hurt invites care.

say: For example, Amaka and her three siblings agreed to send 20,000 naira each month for their mother. Her brother Obi has missed two months. Her first draft was, Obi you are so selfish.

panel.heading: A sister and a family contribution
items: Observation: no share for August, September
Feeling: worried and a bit tired
Need: Mama cared for; sharing fairly
Request: tell me by Sunday what you can send

say: Instead she starts with the observation. Obi, for August and September, I didn't see your 20,000 naira for Mama in the family account.

say: then the need. Because I want Mama to have what she needs, and I need us to share this fairly as we agreed.

say: If a no leads to sulking or punishment, it was a demand. Obi explains he lost a contract and can send 10,000 naira now. Use your own words and language.

say: The negotiation expert William Ury describes a respectful no in three parts. For example, Zainab's cousin asks to borrow 150,000 naira.
First, a yes to what matters to her: her shop money for her children's school fees.

cards.d: 'I'm keeping all my money in the shop this year for my children's school fees.'
'So I can't lend you the 150,000 naira.'
'What I can do is ask my supplier if he needs a sales boy.'

say: Second, a short, clear no. So I can't lend you the money.

cards.d: 'I'm keeping all my money in the shop this year for my children's school fees.'
'So I can't lend you the 150,000 naira.'
'What I can do is ask my supplier if he needs a sales boy.'

say: Third, an offer she truly means. I can ask my supplier if he needs a sales boy. Her cousin is disappointed, but not insulted, and her stock stays safe.

cards.d: 'I'm keeping all my money in the shop this year for my children's school fees.'
'So I can't lend you the 150,000 naira.'
'What I can do is ask my supplier if he needs a sales boy.'

say: Often the first no is not accepted. Repeat your main sentence in the same calm tone. I understand. I still can't lend the money. Each new excuse gives the other person something to argue with.

panel.heading: Staying firm, staying kind
items: Calm repetition, without new excuses
Agree with any truth; keep your decision
Ask for time: I'll tell you tomorrow
One honest reason is enough
Threats or harm? Safety comes first

say: Agree with any part that is true, without changing your decision. You're right, I helped Ifeoma last year. I still can't do it this time.

say: You do not have to answer on the spot. Let me think about it and tell you tomorrow.

say: Do not over-explain. You do not owe anyone a list of your expenses. With elders, greet properly and choose a private moment.

say: If someone answers a respectful no with threats or harm, return to the safety guidance in Module 1, and talk to someone you trust.

say: To remember. Listen, paraphrase and summarise. Say what happened, how you feel, what you need, and what you ask. Give a positive no.
Some guilt after your first few noes is normal. If your reason is still true, the no stands.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Paraphrase and summarise so she can correct you
Observation, feeling, need, request
Ignored or betrayed are accusations, not feelings
Yes to your reason, a clear no, then an offer
Some guilt after a fair no is normal

say: Your practice: hold two listening conversations this week, turn one complaint into a four-line NVC message, and prepare three positive noes, practising them aloud with a trusted friend.
